requirements.title: A component's individual array specification takes precedence over DIMENSION
requirements.source: 7.5.4.2 p1; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 94, printed 80, lines 23-26.
requirements.definition: An individual component-array-spec or a statement-level DIMENSION clause makes the data component an array. If the individual declarator has a specification, that specification determines rank and, for explicit shape, bounds; otherwise the DIMENSION specification does so. The containing object can be scalar while the component is an array. The rule does not give unallocated or unassociated deferred-shape arrays defined bounds.
requirements.oracle: Five initialized runs check individual and shared rank/bounds, per-component rank and bound overrides, and a zero-extent array beside a defined scalar. Nonzero arrays have exact small LBOUND/UBOUND/SHAPE checks. The empty array is never indexed and is not given a false declared-lower-bound inquiry expectation.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Every written component-array-spec must independently satisfy R740/C750/C754/C755 even if an individual suffix overrides a shared specification. A valid active shape does not legalize an invalid unused one. Deferred-shape allocation/association and default initialization are canonical dependencies, not new obligations manufactured from the notes. Preserve runs if implementations lack the feature.
requirements.dependencies: R738-R740/C750/C754/C755 (PDF 93); 8.5.8.2-.4 (PDF 125-126); RANK, SHAPE, SIZE, LBOUND and UBOUND with their zero-extent and allocation/association qualifications (PDF 449, 456, 459, 425, 469); 7.5.4.6/R743/C767 (PDF 96-98); allocation/association (PDF 160-165, 195-196); 19.6.1-.2/19.6.5 (PDF 562-563); 4.2 p2(1) (PDF 46).

accounting.rationale: PDF 94 below p1: the complete LINE definition and LINE_SEGMENT declaration are illustrative context. The note continues on PDF 95 as the separate census unit note1.2.
The example is an ordinary derived type; it is not a new type-class or layout requirement.
The explicit two-by-two coordinate array illustrates statement DIMENSION and component rank. Its comments are not input data that initialize coordinates.
WIDTH and PATTERN are scalar members; sample meanings of numerical values are application conventions, not mandatory processor values.
The scalar LINE_SEGMENT declaration establishes a containing object; no member is initialized by the illustrative comments.
PDF 95, NOTE 1 continuation: array subobject of a scalar and the separate required/optional double-colon cases. This continuation is not lost or combined with NOTE 2.
The component's rank is not the rank of its scalar containing variable.
COORD has a DIMENSION attribute, so its double-colon separator is required by the actual component grammar.
WIDTH and PATTERN have neither component attributes nor initialization in the example; their double colons are optional. This is not a waiver of C766 for initializers.
PDF 95: STACK contains an allocatable array, whose shape can be established through three specified mechanisms. The note supplies context, not a separate locally owned allocation catalogue.
The scalar INDEX and deferred-shape ALLOCATABLE CONTENTS are distinct components; no initial INDEX value or CONTENTS shape is specified.

Canonical 9.7.1.1-.3 (PDF 160-164) establishes shape after successful allocation. A later graph should bind one two-element allocation with explicit status handling, not assume success or query unallocated bounds.

Canonical intrinsic assignment, 10.2.1.3, controls allocation/reallocation from a defined array expression. It is not an assertion about an unallocated array's prior shape; source-valid assignment effects retain their existing owner.

8.5.8.4 and 15.5.2 retain the actual effective-argument and parameter premises. Pending finite graph: pass an initialized scalar STACK object with an allocated two-element CONTENTS component to a TYPE(STACK), INTENT(IN) dummy, check allocation before its component shape, and bind that shape to the effective object's component. A bare unrelated array dummy is not a second local component effect.

PDF 95: default initialization of explicit-shape components uses the constant-expression and assignment premises of 7.5.4.6. This note does not expand the initializer grammar or allow nonconstant LEN-dependent initialized shapes.
The initializer is constant and all applicable type parameters and bounds meet C767. R743/C766-C767 retain ownership; the planned use graph includes a constant two-element declaration only.
A constant array constructor such as a two-element INTEGER value can initialize a conforming component shape through 7.5.4.6 p6 and 10.2.1.3. Canonical 7.8/10.1.12 supply constructor constancy.
A single scalar constant supplies each array element through the canonical initialization/intrinsic-assignment rules, not by a promise of byte filling or contiguous physical storage.
